Financial targets for 2026–2027, based on baseline assumptions as of March 5, 2026, and following the completion on March 30, 2026, of the legislation regarding a special bank tax in 2026 and 2027:
Net profit in the range of NIS 8.5–9.5 billion for 2026 and NIS 9.5–10.5 billion for 2027;
Return on equity in the range of 13%–14% for 2026 and 14%–15% for 2027;
Growth of the credit portfolio at an average annual rate of 8%–9%;
Profit distribution at a rate of 50%–60% of net profit, through cash dividends or buybacks, subject to the guidelines of the Bank of Israel.

Annual general meeting of shareholdersOn October 29, 2026, the bank held its annual general meeting of shareholders for 2026, at which the following resolutions were passed: (1) the Financial Statements and the Report of the Board of Directors and Board of Management of the Bank for 2025 were discussed; (2) the reappointment of Somekh Chaikin (KPMG), CPA, and Ziv Haft (BDO), CPA, as joint auditors of the bank until the end of the next annual general meeting was approved; (3) the appointment of Michal Halperin and Tamar Schechter as external directors pursuant to the Companies Law (for a second and first term of office, respectively) was approved; (4) the appointment of Israel Trau as an other (non-external) director (for a third term of office) was approved; (5) the remuneration policy for officers of the bank was approved; (6) updated terms of service for the bank's directors, in connection with the grant of fixed equity compensation, were approved; and (7) updated terms of service and employment for the Bank's CEO, Yadin Antebi, were approved.As part of the approved remuneration resolutions (items 5 and 7), and as part of a bank-wide initiative to discontinue early retirement arrangements, the option for senior executives to convert their accrued retirement rights into bank shares was also approved.The bank estimates that the conversion of the accrued retirement rights will result in a one-time expense of approximately NIS 8 million. At the same time, discontinuing the accrual of early retirement and enhanced severance rights and converting them into the bank's shares is expected to reduce future expenses (service cost and interest) by approximately NIS 10 million per year.

Bank shares buyback planOn November 19, 2025, the board of directors of the bank (after receiving the approval of the Banking Supervision Department) approved a plan for a buyback of shares of the bank, at a volume not to exceed NIS 1 billion, until November 5, 2026, or until the full amount of the plan was acquired, whichever was earlier. Within this plan, which was completed on September 17, 2026, the bank purchased a cumulative 13,128,375 ordinary shares of the bank, constituting approximately 0.98% of the issued and paid-up capital of the bank, at a total cost of approximately NIS 985 million.On November 15, 2026, the board of directors of the bank approved a new plan for a buyback of shares of the bank at a volume not to exceed NIS 1 billion, from November 17, 2026, until November 1, 2027, or until the full amount of the plan is acquired, whichever is earlier.

Bank Hapoalim will host a conference call/webinar today to discuss the results. The call will take place at 5:00 p.m. Israel time / 3:00 p.m. UK time / 10:00 a.m. Eastern time. Participation in the call/webinar is available via the following link: BankHapoalimQ3.2026 (pre-registration is also available via the link). No password or access code is required. The review will be conducted in listen-only mode, followed by a Q&A session.

The webinar will be accompanied by a presentation, which will be published on the day of the financial statements' release on the distribution website of the Israel Securities Authority (MAGNA), the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange website, and the bank's Investor Relations page (Financial Information section) at: https://www.bankhapoalim.com.
A recording of the conference call/webinar will be available one business day following the event, on the bank's Investor Relations page at the above-mentioned address.
